MINUTES
  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 17, 2019

  1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT: Schmitz, Zuckerman, Addleman, Arata, Carman,
  Carrese, Corman, Friedman, Medawar, Seamans, Shinn,
  Silvano

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Bayer, Buresh, Portugal, Stegura

  STUDENT MEMBERS PRESENT:  Michael Wagreich

  STAFF PRESENT: Greg Grammer, City Manager
  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager,
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  John Bellas, Principal, Michael Baker International
  Shane Burkhardt, Project Manager, Michael Baker International
  Surabhi Barbhaya, Senior Planner, Michael Baker International

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  Approval of General Plan Advisory Committee Meeting Minutes, March 13, 2019

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  MARCH 13, 2019.

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON AGENDA

  NONE

  5.  WELCOME BACK AND INTRODUCTIONS

  A.  Introduction of the New Consulting Team, Michael Baker International (MBI)

  Director Wahba introduced and welcomed the new consultants from Michael Baker International.
  Committee Members, staff, and consultants made their introductions.

  6.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  Where Were We, Where Are We, Moving Forward (City Staff, MBI, GPAC)

  Shane Burkhardt, Michael Baker International provided a brief review of what the GPAC has accomplished
  thus far and how it will be built upon going forward.

  Mr. Burkhardt mentioned that the survey that was sent to the GPAC is essentially a condensed version of
  the existing General Plan and will help to provide a general consensus on the parts that are still applicable.

  B.  Roles and Responsibilities of the GPAC, City, and Consultant (City Staff/MBI)

  Mr. Burkhardt stated that MBI will be providing more information in terms of education, best practices,
  case studies, and information that will be used in agenda item discussions. A list of resources used to
  gather information presented by MBI will be provided to the GPAC.

  (Item discussed out of order)

General Plan Advisory Committee  1
Meeting Minutes, September 17, 2019
   D.  Schedule, Meeting Materials, Information, Archives, and Documents (MBI)
  Mr. Burkhardt stated that the General Plan Update website will be reconstructed and available soon. He
  provided a general overview on accessing Microsoft Teams GPAC and stated that problems with the site
  will be addressed. In addition, hard copies will be provided for those who prefer this method for delivery
  of documents.

  The next meetings have been confirmed to be held on Tuesday, October 15, November 19, and December
  17, 2019 at 6:30 p.m.

  C.  General Plan Preview (MBI)

  Mr. Burkhardt shared that the Office of Planning and Research has a website,
  (http://opr.ca.gov/planning/general-plan/guidelines.html), on the General Plan and all of the Elements.

  Mr. Burkhardt provided a presentation with an overview of the General Plan, its purpose, required
  elements, and optional elements.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER MEDAWAR, Mr. Burkhardt stated that although retail
  is not a required element, it can fit under Land Use in terms of where retail can be located. It can also fit
  under Economic Development as an optional element.

  Mr. Burkhardt stated that the Land Use Element is the official land use map for the City and will be utilized
  when making changes to the zoning ordinance, future specific plans, discretionary approvals, etc., and
  will need to be in harmony with the General Plan.

  In response to a question by STUDENT MEMBER WAGREICH, Mr. Burkhardt stated that education can
  be an element, however, the General Plan is specific to city government and we need to be careful about
  policies that may impact other agencies.

  John Bellas, Michael Baker International, added that municipal city governments and school districts have
  two different elected bodies; the school district will have a Master Plan. Mr. Burkhardt further added that
  education related elements could be included as recommendations. Office of Planning and Research
  encourages municipalities to be in coordination and consultation with school districts when discussing land
  use.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Mr. Burkhardt stated that the
  Community Development Element may include, among others: land use, urban design, environmental
  justice issues, disadvantaged communities, or affordable housing.

  Mr. Burkhardt stated that Transportation must be looked at in a way to move people and not vehicles. He
  further explained Senate Bill 743.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that there will be times when the City does not have a choice since the State
  mandates what can be done with certain items that will be discussed.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER ZUCKERMAN asked to what degree congestion guidelines or principles can be
  a part of the General Plan. Mr. Bellas stated that with passing SB 743, legislature is saying that traffic
  congestion cannot be considered significant impact in a CEQA document; however, a local agency could
  still address it in a General Plan. Mr. Burkhardt stated that this item will be included as part of a future
  discussion.

  Mr. Burkhardt stated that previously, the goal was to have the General Plan Update completed prior to
  updating the Housing Element, but now are at a point when they will be worked on simultaneously and
  MBI will be helping to coordinate this.

  Mr. Burkhardt explained the Conservation Element focuses on preserving the cultural and biological
  resources, air quality, and scenic viewsheds.

  Mr. Burkhardt further explained what is required in the Open Space and Recreation, Noise, and Public
  Safety Elements. Optional Elements explained were, Economic Development and Sustainability.

  E.  Survey – Exploration and Assessment of the Current General Plan (MBI)

  Mr. Burkhardt stated that the current goals and policies are part of the survey, which was already sent to
  the GPAC.

Meeting Minutes, September 17, 2019
   7.  CONSULTANT ITEMS

  Mr. Burkhardt stated that there are two homework assignments for the GPAC:
  1. Survey sent by MBI via Survey Monkey.
  2. Review the draft Vision and Guiding Principles, which will be sent from staff, and prepare
  comments and bring to the next meeting.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER CORMAN suggested that copies of the laws that will be discussed in future
  meetings be provided ahead of time. Mr. Burkhardt stated that educational information will be available on
  the TEAMS site.

  8.  COMMITTEE ITEMS

  Suzy Seamans stated that she would like to see actual RHE photos used in presentations and materials.
  Mr. Burkhardt stated that RHE photos will be used in all materials with the exception of various Case
  Studies.

  9.  STAFF ITEMS

  NONE

  10.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 8:02 p.m. The next General Plan Advisory Committee
  Meeting is schedule on Tuesday, October 15, 2019 at 6:30 p.m. in the City of Rolling Hills Estates’
  Council Chamber, located at 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.
